hook.line: Don Hernando loves telling how much he ate, read or drank in one go. Spanish has a small extra word for "the whole thing, and I enjoyed it".

examples.es: Me leí el libro en una noche.
examples.en: I read the whole book in one night.

examples.es: Se tomó dos cervezas y se fue.
examples.en: He downed two beers and left.
Did you drink all the coffee?

examples.es: Vale se aprendió la receta en una tarde.
examples.en: Vale learned the whole recipe in one afternoon.

rule:
Add *me*, *te*, *se* or *nos* before the verb, matching the person doing it: *me leí*, *te tomaste*, *se aprendió*, *nos comimos*.

It does not mean "myself". It says: all of it, finished, and I was involved. English gets this from words like "whole", "down" or "every last".

It works with eating, drinking, reading, learning and spending, and the thing must be a whole, counted or measured thing: *un pollo*, *dos cervezas*, *el libro*, *todo el tinto*.

Bare, open-ended things do not fit: *me comí pollo* sounds wrong, *me comí un pollo* is fine.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the aspectual dative: a pronoun that adds completeness and personal involvement, not a reflexive action.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ tomaste todo el tinto.* (*Te* or *Se*) You drank all the coffee (to a friend).
yourTurn.why: You is *tú* here, so the pronoun is *te*, matching *tomaste*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ comimos todos los buñuelos.* (*Nos* or *Me*) We ate every last buñuelo.
yourTurn.why: The pronoun matches the person: *nos* goes with *comimos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I read the whole book in one night.
yourTurn.answer: Me leí el libro en una noche.
yourTurn.why: *Me* plus the verb says you finished the whole book.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I ate a whole chicken.
yourTurn.why: A whole chicken is a bounded thing, so *me comí* fits.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Vale learned the whole recipe in one afternoon.
yourTurn.answer: Vale se aprendió la receta en una tarde.
accept: Vale se aprendió toda la receta en una tarde.
yourTurn.why: The pronoun *se* goes with Vale, who did it.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Did you read the whole contract?
yourTurn.why: *Te* matches *tú*, and *el contrato completo* is a whole thing.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about me: *Se tomó dos cervezas y se fue.* becomes: I downed two beers and left.
yourTurn.answer: Me tomé dos cervezas y me fui.
yourTurn.why: Both verbs change person, so both pronouns change to *me*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. This *me* wants a whole, countable thing: *un pollo*, not just "chicken".

pitfalls.wrong: Se leí el libro en una noche.
pitfalls.right: Me leí el libro en una noche.
pitfalls.why: The pronoun has to match the person: I read, so *me*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me leía el libro en una noche.
pitfalls.right: Me leí el libro en una noche.
pitfalls.why: Finishing the whole book is a completed action, so it takes the preterite, *leí*.

personal: Tell us about something you finished in one go: a book, a meal, a series. Use *me* plus the verb: *Me vi…*, *Me comí…*
